descriptionChirho: A causal conjunction introducing the reason or ground for a preceding statement, equivalent to 'because' or 'for.' This is the dominant sense (21 of 23 occurrences). Spanish 'porque,' Hindi 'kyonki,' Arabic 'li'anna,' Korean 'waenyahamyeon,' Swahili 'kwa sababu.' Used extensively in Pauline and Petrine epistles to provide theological grounding for exhortations (e.g., Rom 1:19 'because God has shown it to them'; 1 Pet 1:16 'because it is written').

An inferential conjunction drawing a conclusion or consequence from what precedes, closer to 'therefore' or 'for this reason' than to simple 'because.' Only 2 occurrences with this sense. Spanish 'por esto/por lo cual,' Hindi 'isliye,' Arabic 'li-dhalika,' Korean 'geureomeuro,' Swahili 'kwa hiyo.' The shift from causal backward-looking reasoning to forward-looking inference distinguishes this from the dominant causal sense, as confirmed by the divergent translation signatures across languages.
